overlap_rationale: Study A (Rout & Kattumuri, 2022; S600) is a 318-page Springer monograph whose text in the prompt is readable from PDF Page 1 through PDF Page 68, where the prompt ends with '<truncated 53508 bytes>'. Because of this truncation inside Study A, '== STUDY B FULL TEXT ==' (Roy, Akshintala & Sharma, 2013; S799) was completely omitted from the prompt and is not accessible. What CAN be verified from Study A's accessible chapters (Preface, Contents, Lists of Figures/Tables, Chapter 1 including Section 1.6 'A Note on Methodology', and Chapter 2) is that Study A analyzes a primary household survey of N = 3,714 urban households across four Indian cities—Ahmedabad (n = 1,000), Bengaluru (n = 1,000), Hyderabad (n = 1,000) and Kochi (n = 714)—funded by a UGC-UKIERI partnership grant (conceived during 2012–2013 at LSE with workshops in June–August 2016), alongside secondary data from the Census of India (2001, 2011), Central Water Commission (2015), ADB (2007) and municipal water utilities (AMC, BWSSB, HMWSSB, KWA). Metadata also show non-overlapping author teams and publication dates nine years apart (Rout & Kattumuri 2022 vs Roy, Akshintala & Sharma 2013). What CANNOT be verified without Study B's full text (and PDF Pages 69–318 of Study A) is whether Study B reports primary fieldwork or secondary urban water statistics (e.g., Census/NSSO/ADB city-level indicators), which Indian cities or utilities Study B examines, its sample size and dates, and whether any empirical tables or secondary series overlap. Per strict audit rules prohibiting guessing from titles/metadata alone when either full text is inaccessible, pair_classification is set to 'cannot_tell_missing_full_text'.
study_a_sample_and_data: Primary household survey of N = 3,714 households across four Indian cities—Ahmedabad (Gujarat, n = 1,000), Bengaluru (Karnataka, n = 1,000), Hyderabad (Telangana, n = 1,000) and Kochi (Kerala, n = 714)—funded by a UGC-UKIERI grant (conceived 2012–2013, workshops in 2016), supplemented by secondary data from Census of India (2001, 2011), Central Water Commission (2015), ADB (2007) and city water utilities (PDF Pages 1–68 of 318 accessible; Pages 69–318 truncated).
